Scenario generator: no limit

Each press adds new scenarios, never the same one twice: correlated shocks across every driver, shaped by the theme, plus shocks to model lines. They are ranked on the agent’s estimate; the worst are then checked in EstateMaster on a scratch copy that the runner restores, so the model does not change.

From napkin to EstateMaster

Each step adds detail without changing the answer: the numbers are the same, now broken down line by line, with the basis for each one and a benchmark from past projects. Edit anything later in Model data.

Model data: every assumption

Edit any line (or ask the agent, e.g. "increase MEP by 10%" or "set contingency to 7%"). Changes go to the sandbox copy and EstateMaster recalculates.

Model lines: every other assumption

No limit on the number of lines: they come from the Lines sheet of the model’s control workbook. The agent has no instant estimate for them, so a change becomes a change request and EstateMaster calculates the effect when it runs. Ask the agent too, e.g. “set pharmacy rent to 2,900”.

Elemental cost plan

Construction lines split into elements. Edit an element and its line in EstateMaster updates (the change is logged).

1
Use the official WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API), through a BSPNot the WhatsApp Business app and not unofficial libraries: those risk account bans and fail a compliance review. A BSP gives templates, delivery receipts and an SLA.
2
WhatsApp is the front door, not the engineAsk, get alerts, approve. Heavy runs happen in the workspace; WhatsApp gets the headline numbers, a chart image and a link to the PDF.
3
Known numbers, mapped rolesAllow-list of KINAN phone numbers tied to a role. Analyst: read and sandbox scenarios. Director: can approve promotion. Try switching the role on the phone and asking to promote.
4
Three permission tiersTier 0 read KPIs · Tier 1 sandbox scenarios and reports · Tier 2 write to the live model needs a Director's approval with a step-up check (one-time code or secure link). The base case is never edited straight from chat.
5
Interactive buttons and pre-approved templatesReply buttons for approvals and choices. Proactive alerts (e.g. "explorer found a hurdle breach") outside the 24-hour window must use approved message templates.
6
Keep raw model data off the chatSend summaries plus an expiring signed link, not full workbooks. Confirm hosting and retention with KINAN compliance (Saudi PDPL). Every message → action → model change is written to an audit log.
7
1:1 with the agent, sharing through the workspaceAvoid group chats for anything that changes numbers; it blurs who asked. Support voice notes for site walks, Arabic and English.

How the agent operates EstateMaster

Every return is calculated by EstateMaster itself. EstateMaster has no API, so inputs and results go through Excel, and the runner presses EstateMaster’s buttons the way an analyst would.
1
Setup, once per model (Copilot)The Copilot setup agent fills the KINAN control workbook from the model’s Office Links export; an analyst checks it and connects it here (Model data → Connect control workbook), as a change request.
2
Write approved inputsAfter approval, the runner (Windows VM with licensed EstateMaster and Excel) writes the values into the control workbook’s fixed cells. Nothing unapproved is written.
3
Operate EstateMasterIt opens the model, presses Office Links → Refresh, recalculates, exports to Excel, saves a copy and closes (Windows UI automation).
4
Read back and reconcileResults are read from EstateMaster’s export by row label, compared with the agent’s estimate and logged against the change request.
5
New models and the live modelNew models are copies of a KINAN master template, created by the runner after approval. Promotion backs up the live model’s workbook, writes the approved values and saves the live model; it needs an Investment Director.
!
Fallback and licenceIf the automation fails, an analyst gets a one-minute task (open, Refresh, Export) and presses Collect. Confirm unattended use with Altus.

Two-speed engine

Why the agent can run "infinite" scenarios
A
Fast estimateAn estimator fitted to EstateMaster’s own results from the runner: instant answers and wide scans (explorer, Monte Carlo, heatmaps), always labelled as estimates. This demo runs on a simplified stand-in.
B
Truth engine: EstateMasterAnything that goes into a report or an IC decision is re-run in EstateMaster by the runner and reconciled to the replica. Findings are flagged "verified" only after that.

Guardrails

Agent only edits a sandbox copy; promotion to the live model is a separate approved step.
Every read, write, recalculation and report is logged with user, channel, data source and timestamp.
Assumption changes are diffed against base and stamped on every report.
Replica drift check: if replica and EstateMaster disagree beyond tolerance, the agent stops and says so.

Outlook integration

How the agent gets context on assumption changes from email
1
Microsoft Graph, read-onlyAn Entra ID app with Mail.Read, limited by an application access policy to one project mailbox or folder (e.g. "Al Narjis"). The agent never sends or deletes mail.
2
Two scans a day07:00 and 15:00 Riyadh time (plus on request), on the server even when nobody has the app open. Each scan reads new mail in the project folder only, and when it senses a possible assumption change it alerts the people on the alert list by email, WhatsApp and the bell.
3
Extract, then proposeThe agent pulls the assumption, the new value and the sentence it came from, and raises a change request. Nothing is written to EstateMaster until a person approves it; promotion to the live model needs an Investment Director.
4
Cited everywhereApplied changes carry the sender, date, subject and quote into the changelog, the IC pack and "why did this change?" answers.

What it reads, what it ignores

Reads: cost plans and tender returns, pricing notes, term sheets, planning feedback, leasing LOIs, programme updates.
Ignores: anything without a model assumption (HR, logistics, newsletters). Attachments are read only from allow-listed senders.
Low-confidence extractions are flagged for a person to confirm before they can be applied.
Mail stays in Microsoft 365; the agent stores only the extracted fields and a message link.

AI providers

No engine choice: the router picks EstateMaster, a data query or an AI model per request, and the model by task across Claude and OpenAI (e.g. GPT-5 mini for commentary, Claude Sonnet for agent work, Claude Opus for IC narratives, GPT-5 for Excel questions), each with a failover on the other provider.
Claude (Anthropic Messages API) and OpenAI (Chat Completions API) can both be connected; if one fails, the other takes over. With neither, the rules engine still answers.
All engines share the same tool set: status, assumptions, stress, sensitivity, headroom, explorer, market, zoning, Outlook, capital structure, Excel, report, promotion request.
Production: keys live on Bohio's gateway, not in the browser; the model never gets write access to the base case.

New model from a previous project

The runner copies the template project's EstateMaster file, clears its project data, and writes the new plot, areas and inputs. The structure (sections, lines, units, cash-flow logic) is kept. Creating the file needs approval.
